_comment: Provenance for the bundled language data. Kept in its own file because kanji_data.json is a bare array with nowhere to put a header. Update the version and retrievedOn whenever the data is re-derived from upstream — the EDRDG licence asks for a procedure for regular updating, and you can't honour that if you can't tell what you're holding.

sources.name: JMdict / EDICT
sources.publisher: Electronic Dictionary Research and Development Group
sources.note: A curated subset scoped to the N5–N1 levels (4,094 entries), not a full copy of upstream. Retrieval date is the earliest commit carrying this file; the exact upstream release was not recorded at the time, so re-derive from a dated upstream file at the next refresh and fill in upstreamVersion then.

sources.name: KANJIDIC
sources.publisher: Electronic Dictionary Research and Development Group
sources.note: A curated subset scoped to the N5–N1 levels (1,103 kanji), not a full copy of upstream. Retrieval date is the earliest commit carrying this file; the exact upstream release was not recorded at the time, so re-derive from a dated upstream file at the next refresh and fill in upstreamVersion then.

sources.name: Tanaka Corpus
sources.publisher: Tatoeba Project, distributed by the Electronic Dictionary Research and Development Group
sources.note: One or two sentences per entry, chosen as the shortest well-formed pair carrying an English translation. Sentences shown with furigana come from this app's own lessons instead.

sources.name: KRADFILE
sources.usedFor: Kanji component breakdowns shown in each kanji card’s insight panel
sources.publisher: Electronic Dictionary Research and Development Group
sources.note: Component glyphs are mapped from KRADFILE’s surrogate characters to their proper radical forms for display; component names and memory aids are original to this app.
